addprimesum: Parse the argument by hand, then test each number from 2 up with trial division up to its square root; invalid, zero or negative input prints `0`.
brackets: Push each opening bracket on a stack and pop when you meet a closer; a mismatch or a non-empty stack at the end means `Error`.
cameltosnakecase: First validate the camelCase rules (no digits, no two capitals in a row, no capital at the end); only then insert `_` before each capital.
canjump: Walk from index 0 jumping exactly the value at each step; you succeed only if you land on the last index, and a 0 before that means you are stuck.
checknumber: Loop over the runes and return true as soon as one falls between '0' and '9'.
chunk: Step through the slice `size` elements at a time, clamping the last chunk to the slice length; handle `size == 0` by printing just a newline.
cleanstr: Treat spaces and tabs as separators: emit a single space only between words, never before the first or after the last.
concatalternate: Decide which slice goes first by length (first slice on a tie), then alternate indexes and append the leftover tail of the longer one.
concatslice: `append` can take a whole slice if you spread it with `...`; make sure empty inputs still work.
countalpha: Count runes that fall in 'a'-'z' or 'A'-'Z'; spaces and digits do not count.
countcharacter: Range over the string comparing each rune to `c`; note `5` is not the same rune as '5'.
digitlen: Check the base range 2..36 first, flip a negative number to positive, then count how many times you can divide by the base before reaching 0.
expandstr: Collect the words separated by spaces/tabs, then print them joined by exactly three spaces; no words or wrong arg count prints nothing.
fifthandskip: Drop the spaces first, then walk the characters taking five, adding a space, and skipping the sixth; check the empty and under-5 cases before anything.
findpairs: Parse the array carefully (validate the format and numbers), then use two nested loops with `j > i` so each pair of indices appears once.
findprevprime: Count down from `nb` and return the first number that passes a primality check; anything below 2 gives 0.
firstword: Skip leading spaces, then collect characters until the next space; remember the trailing newline even for an empty string.
fishandchips: Check the negative case first, and test divisibility by both 2 and 3 before testing each one alone.
fprime: Divide by the smallest factor repeatedly starting at 2, printing `*` only between factors; 0, 1 and invalid input print nothing.
fromto: Validate both bounds first, then count up or down depending on which is larger, padding single digits with a leading `0`.
gcd: Euclid's algorithm repeatedly replaces the pair with (b, a mod b); return 0 early if either input is 0.
hashcode: Use the string length in the formula for every character, and add 33 when the result lands in the unprintable range (below 32 or 127).
hiddenp: Use one index into `s1` and advance it whenever the current char of `s2` matches; an empty `s1` is always hidden.
inter: For each char of the first string, print it if it appears in the second and hasn't been printed yet.
iscapitalized: Split on spaces and check only the first character of each word with a lowercase test; an empty string returns false.
itoa: Build digits with `% 10` and `/ 10` from the end, handle 0 and the minus sign separately.
itoabase: Index into the digit string "0123456789ABCDEF" with `n % base`, building in reverse; take care with the sign and with 0.
lastword: Trim trailing spaces first, then scan backwards to the previous space; a string of only spaces returns just `\n`.
notdecimal: If it does not parse as a number, return it as-is; otherwise count the digits after the `.` and multiply by 10 to that power. End every result with `\n`.
only1: A single call to `z01.PrintRune` is all you need, with no newline.
onlya: A single call to `z01.PrintRune` is all you need, with no newline.
onlyb: A single call to `z01.PrintRune` with an uppercase letter, and no newline.
onlyf: A single call to `z01.PrintRune` is all you need, with no newline.
onlyz: A single call to `z01.PrintRune` is all you need, with no newline.
options: Map each letter to a bit with `1 << (letter - 'a')` and OR them together; `-h` or no arguments prints the usage, and a bad letter is an invalid option.
piglatin: Find the index of the first vowel (both cases): 0 means just add "ay", none means "No vowels", otherwise rotate the prefix to the end.
printif: Compare `len(str)` against 3, and remember the empty string is a special case that also returns `G`.
printifnot: A single length comparison decides the result; the empty string falls on the `G` side.
printrevcomb: Three nested loops counting down where each inner digit is strictly smaller than the outer one; only print `, ` between combinations.
rectperimeter: Reject any negative side with -1 before applying the perimeter formula.
repeatalpha: A letter's repeat count is its position from 'a' (or 'A') plus one; non-letters are copied once.
retainfirsthalf: Slicing up to `len(str)/2` rounds down automatically; strings of length 0 or 1 come back unchanged.
revconcatalternate: Walk both slices from their ends; while the longer one has extra elements take from it, then alternate starting with the first slice.
reversestrcap: Lowercase every letter, then uppercase a letter when the next character is a space or the end of the string.
revwstr: Split the string on spaces and print the words from last to first, joined by single spaces.
romannumbers: Use a table of values including the subtractive pairs (900, 400, 90, 40, 9, 4), and reject 0, non-numbers and values ≥ 4000.
rostring: Collect the words, then print from the second word onward and put the first word last, single-spaced.
rpncalc: Use a stack: push numbers, and on an operator pop two operands (mind their order); the stack must hold exactly one value at the end, and `/` or `%` by 0 is an error.
saveandmiss: Step through the string in blocks of `num`, keeping every other block; return the input unchanged when `num <= 0`.
searchreplace: Check for exactly 3 arguments, then print each rune of the first, swapping it when it equals the second argument's letter.
slice: Convert negative indices by adding the length, clamp to bounds, and return nil when the start ends up after the end.
thirdtimeisacharm: Pick the characters at indexes 2, 5, 8, …; if there are none, return just a newline.
union: Walk both strings in order and print each character the first time you see it, tracking seen chars in a map or array.
wdmatch: Advance a pointer through the first string each time the second string's char matches; print only if you reached the end.
weareunique: Gather the distinct characters of each string, count those that appear in only one; both empty is the special -1 case.
wordflip: Use `strings.Fields` to normalise spaces, then join the words back in reverse; an empty input returns `Invalid Output`.
zipstring: Count each run of consecutive identical letters and output the count followed by the letter.
